source: this repo, 2026-11-06 — the bug release-intelligence/scripts/risk.py had on its first draft, caught by its own test
why_this_case_exists: Two migration statements that look alike and are not. `ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL` with no DEFAULT is rejected by Postgres on a non-empty table: a failed deploy. The same statement WITH a DEFAULT is safe and routine. A reviewer that cannot tell them apart either misses the broken one or blocks every additive migration, and both make it useless.

expected.why: ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no DEFAULT fails on a non-empty table
a deployment rollback restores the code and leaves the schema — the change is not reversible by a revert

traps.why: ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EUR' is safe and additive. Flagging it is the false positive that makes a migration reviewer get switched off
